newsitem.title: NORWAY: NatWest says upgrades Kvaerner to buy.
newsitem.headline: NatWest says upgrades Kvaerner to buy.

text.p: NatWest Securities said on Thursday it was upgrading Norwegian group Kvaerner ASA from hold to buy following the release of the 1996 results this week.
"The share price potential is substantial if the group emerges in a debt-free and restructured state," a results analysis said.
"The average P/E range for the peer group is 15-20, suggesting a potential doubling of the share price. We upgrade from hold to buy," NatWest said.
The Kvarner A share fell 2.5 percent, or 8.50 crowns, to finish at 335 crowns on the Oslo Bourse on Thursday, the day after the release of annual profits which fell short of expectations.
Kvaerner on Tuesday booked 1996 operating profits at 1.03 billion crowns, down 48 percent from a year ago, and said it did not foresee any improvement until the second half of 1997.
NatWest said: "Group operating profit should improve substantially this year and management aims to cut net debt to zero by the end of 1998 through continued disposals of non-core assets.

"An improved economic outlook and a recovery in the Pulping Division should boost group pre-tax profit margin towards the 3-4 percent level and EPS towards 50 crowns over the next couple of years," it said.

"By far the most important features in the 1996 results statement were the continued steady performance of the old 'Trafalgar' divisions and the recent breakthrough in the international FPSO market for the Oil & Gas Division," the analysis said.
The London-based engineering and construction group, which acquired Britain's Trafalgar House in April, said turnover doubled to 58.56 billion crowns, against 30.19 billion crowns a year earlier.
But operating expenses rose to 56.20 billion crowns from 27.33 billion crowns. Pre-tax profits amounted to 750 million crowns versus 2.44 billion crowns.

NatWest saw evidence of improving market fundamentals in a number of Kvaerner's core divisions "and it is now also clear that Kvaerner is certain to find the Trafalgar House acquisition far more rewarding than was the case for HK Land".
"The order intake is developing nicely and profitability should follow, although near-term earnings are likely to progress in a volatile manner," the analysis said.
